description: FamilySearch tree person read for Patrick Flynn WITH relatives and source descriptions — the only init-project fixture that exercises the relationship import, the FAN rule, and the multi-person re-ID to local I/N/F/R/S ids. Wife Mary Kelly, children James and Margaret; no parents, because the parents are the research target. Names and relationships arrive without ids, per simplified-gedcomx-spec.md §3 — the caller mints them. Each person does carry an `ark` and each name a `preferred: true`, which person_read always emits: the ark is the only field surviving the re-ID that still points at the FamilySearch person, so dropping it during the copy leaves every tree person unlinked. Facts carry both tool-emitted sidecars (`standard_place`, `standard_date`), neither a string copy of its raw field. One source description carries a `notes` array: person_read emits it, TREE_SOURCE_FIELDS rejects it, so a verbatim copy into the tree fails the project_create write and dropping the whole source to dodge that is the wrong fix. Extended with Patrick's source-style MEMORIES, which this tool returns in the same sources[] array for a non-living subject: memory 228755097 is a family story carrying its full text in `text` (a story's payload text is only a 200-character preview, so the full words come from its artifact), and memory 175960782 is a headstone scan the read's transcription budget did not reach — it still comes back, as metadata whose `notes` says why, and its research.json source takes `transcription: null`. Two further memories on this person are ABSENT ON PURPOSE and their absence is part of what this fixture asserts: the designated portrait, and a family snapshot filed under Photos. Both are dropped by the tool-side filter before the response is built, so a skill must never expect them. Note that the filter is a proxy on media kind — the uploader chooses that kind — so it will also miss a record scan filed under Photos. Both memory sources carry `artifact_url`, the memory ARTIFACT url, which is what `image_transcribe`/`image_read` accept as `memoryArtifactUrl` -- `url` is the human /memories/<id> page and is refused. Like `notes` and `text` it is RESPONSE-ONLY: `TREE_SOURCE_FIELDS` is {id, title, citation, author, url}, so a verbatim copy of one of these rows into tree.gedcomx.json fails the project_create write, and the skill must drop it. Row 175960782 is the budget-skipped memory whose note names that retry route, so without artifact_url the note pointed at a value the row did not contain.

sources.title: Patrick Flynn, as remembered by his granddaughter
sources.text: Patrick came over from County Mayo in 1867, a boy of nineteen with his brother Michael. He went into the Schuylkill mines that same winter. He never spoke of the crossing, my mother said, except once, that the water had been very bad. He married Mary Kelly at St. Patrick's in Pottsville and they had the two children, James and Margaret. He was a quiet man and a hard worker, and he died of the miner's asthma in 1908.
